chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn al-Walid al-Wassafi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The people of kindness in the world are the people of kindness in the Hereafter, and the people of evil deeds in the world are the people of evil deeds in the Hereafter.'
ai.seo_question: What is the connection between good deeds in this world and the Hereafter according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) via the Prophet (PBUH) underscores the principle of *Taba'iyah* (consequence), where one's dominant character traits in the dunya become their defining identity in the akhira. It serves as a foundational teaching in Shia ethics, linking the continuity of the self across the two worlds and emphasizing that habitual actions shape eternal recognition.
